doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Mangione's melodies, bandmates, Gerry Niewood and Don Alias
summary: Frichtel values Mangione's melodic gift, recalls Niewood, Vadala and Coleman Mellett (killed in a plane crash), and befriends Don Alias.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: He’s a controversial figure. Some people think he was like the Kenny G of his day. But he wrote such great hooks.

Yeah. I think his greatest strength was exactly what you just touched on. The melodies and the music to me personally were deeper than the modern day smooth jazzers. And I just thought he had a wonderful sense of melody and harmony and of course he’s a wonderful flugelhornist himself and hey, he played with Art Blakey you know. And he and Gerry Niewood had a special thing. I mean growing up together and playing all those years that they had together. I was lucky enough to play most of the time Gerry was there, but when he wasn’t there Chris Vadala was there. And we had a great band. It was really great. At first Grant was still doing some of the gigs, Grant Geissman, and then we got a wonderful young guitarist who became one of my dearest friends, a guy named Coleman Mellett who sadly he and Gerry were killed when —

The flight went down outside of Buffalo. But we had great bands. And I finally, after hearing this guy on record and hearing about him from Carmen and Ricky, I finally got to meet Don Alias. Because Don was in the band. And Don and I became fast friends, I think mostly because I knew Ricky and Carmen. And boy, talk about, as Corey Allen, our keyboardist said one time, he says, “Don just flies at a different altitude.” And it was true. We would play, we always did “Amazing Grace.” And Don was just playing some kind of like tambourine thing on three. But it was great. And his soloing and his whole approach, he was just a fun, fun guy. I love him and I really miss him.
